samples.summary: `redirect: 'manual'` may produce an opaque-redirect response, breaking every redirecting image URL
samples.evidence: `const res = await fetchImpl(current, { redirect: 'manual' });` then `REDIRECT_STATUSES.has(res.status) ? res.headers.get('location') : null`. Per the Fetch Standard, redirect mode "manual" yields an *opaque-redirect filtered response*: `status === 0`, empty header list, null body. If the Node runtime the CLI ships on implements that filtering (undici has historically gone back and forth on this), `res.status` is 0, `location` is null, `res.ok` is false, and the loop throws `Image fetch failed: 0  for <url>` — so a CDN/S3 `302` (the normal case for stored blobs) makes `docs export`/`slides export` fail instead of following the hop. Every redirect test in `packages/cli/test/image-fetcher.test.ts` injects a hand-built `Response` with a real 302 status and headers, so a stub can never surface this; nothing exercises the real `fetch`.

samples.summary: Redirect response bodies are never consumed or cancelled in the manual-redirect loop
samples.evidence: On each hop the code reads only `res.headers.get('location')` and moves on (`current = next`), and on the `hop >= MAX_IMAGE_REDIRECTS` path it throws, leaving `res.body` unread. With `redirect: 'manual'` the caller now owns each intermediate response; undici keeps the socket/stream around until the body is consumed or cancelled, so a long chain (or a redirect with a body) can retain connections for the life of the export. Previously `fetch` followed redirects internally and drained them.

samples.summary: Any upstream message beginning with `<` is discarded wholesale, including legitimate text
samples.evidence: `if (!trimmed || trimmed.startsWith('<')) return null;` — the HTML heuristic is a single leading character. A real backend/class-validator message such as `"<empty> is not a valid range"` or `"<doc-id> must be a string"` is dropped, and `forwardUpstreamError`/`upstreamErrorJson` then report a bare `HTTP <status>` with no detail — the exact information loss this helper was introduced to prevent.

samples.summary: `isErrorEnvelope` accepts an empty-string `code`, contradicting `errorCode`'s own contract
samples.evidence: `typeof (err as {code?: unknown}).code === 'string'` admits `{ error: { code: '' } }`, which is then forwarded verbatim as "the documented envelope" and printed with `code: ""`. `errorCode` (line 44) explicitly requires `code.length > 0` before treating a thrown error's code as usable, so the two paths disagree: the same degenerate body yields `code: ""` through `forwardUpstreamError` and `HTTP_ERROR` through the throwing path — the branch-on-`code` invariant this change is built around.

samples.summary: `safeEnvelope`'s oversize fallback invents a `message` the upstream never sent
samples.evidence: For a body with no `error.message`, the small-body branch returns the envelope without a `message` key, but the >4000-byte branch returns `{ error: { code, message: error.message ?? `HTTP ${status}` } }` — synthesizing `"HTTP 500"` as if the backend had said it. The same input therefore produces two different documented shapes depending only on how much unrelated debug context the backend attached.

samples.summary: An IPv6 entry in WAFFLEBASE_IMAGE_HOSTS can never match, so the documented escape hatch is unusable for IPv6 hosts
samples.evidence: `isAllowedHost` compares operator entries against `url.host` (`[::1]:9000`) and `url.hostname` (`[::1]`), both of which keep the WHATWG brackets, while `parseAllowedHosts` only trims/lowercases — an operator writing `::1` or `fd00::5:9000` (the natural spelling, and the one `[..]` would be stripped from nowhere) never matches, so `assertFetchableImageUrl` refuses an explicitly allowed IPv6 blob host and the export fails with no way to opt in.

samples.summary: A 2xx response with no bytes is reported as an upstream HTTP error with a nonsense `HTTP 200` message
samples.evidence: `if (!res.ok || !res.bytes) { io.stderr(upstreamErrorJson(res)); ... }` — when the request succeeded but `bytes` is missing, `upstreamErrorJson({status: 200, data: undefined})` emits `{error:{code:'HTTP_ERROR', message:'HTTP 200'}}`. The new helper makes this louder than the old `{error:{code:'HTTP_ERROR'}}` while still describing a success status as an HTTP failure, giving an agent a code/message pair that cannot be acted on.

samples.summary: `bareFilename` does not reduce Windows-style paths on POSIX
samples.evidence: `basename(name)` uses the platform separator, so on POSIX a `Content-Disposition` filename or docId of `..\\..\\.bashrc` is returned intact as a single "bare filename" containing backslashes. The comment above claims the value is "reduced to a bare filename before it can reach the filesystem"; that holds only for the running platform's separator, so the guard's stated invariant is weaker than advertised for cross-platform inputs.

verdict.reason: The cited code is present exactly as described: image-fetcher.ts:221 issues `fetchImpl(current, { redirect: 'manual' })` and lines 222-224 read `res.status`/`res.headers.get('location')` to detect the hop. Under the Fetch Standard, redirect mode "manual" produces an opaque-redirect filtered response (status 0, empty header list, null body); with such a response `REDIRECT_STATUSES.has(0)` is false, `location` is null, `res.ok` is false, and lines 226-231 throw `Image fetch failed: 0  for <url>` instead of following the redirect. The production path uses the real runtime fetch (line 207 defaults to `globalThis.fetch`; packages/cli/package.json:10-11 targets Node >=20), and docs/design/cli.md:1135-1138 states following the Location hop is the intended behavior, so a CDN/S3 302 would break `docs export`/`slides export`. I could not establish any refutation ground: the code is present, no caller or fallback re-issues the request with `redirect: 'follow'` (this is the only `redirect: 'manual'` site in non-node_modules sources), and no undici source is vendored in the tree with which to demonstrate a non-filtering runtime. The redirect tests in packages/cli/test/image-fetcher.test.ts:257-327 all inject hand-built Responses with real 302 statuses and headers, so they cannot surface the filtered-response case. This is a runtime-correctness/logic failure (mis-handled response breaking a core flow), squarely in this lens.

finding.summary: `seg()` guard added only to documents.ts; every other frontend API module still interpolates raw ids into request paths
finding.evidence: The new `packages/frontend/src/api/url.ts` guard is applied in `api/documents.ts` only. Grepping `${import.meta.env.VITE_BACKEND_API_URL}...${...}` shows unguarded interpolations still reaching `fetchWithAuth` at `api/folders.ts:10,24,42,64,82` (`/folders/${id}`, `/workspaces/${workspaceId}/folders`), `api/share-links.ts:60,78,89,102` (`/documents/${documentId}/share-links`, `/share-links/${id}`, `/share-links/${token}/resolve`), `api/analytics.ts:127`, `api/miro.ts:93`, `api/workspaces.ts:156`. A `..`/`/`-bearing id on any of those paths still walks the session-carrying request onto a different endpoint — the exact condition the guard was introduced to remove — so the invariant the new test in `documents.test.ts` asserts does not actually hold for the client as a whole.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `seg()` is applied only in `api/documents.ts` and that other API modules interpolate raw ids. Every location it cites as unguarded actually calls `seg()`. `api/folders.ts` imports `seg` at line 4 and uses it at all five cited lines (11, 25, 43, 65, 83). `api/share-links.ts` imports `seg` at line 3 and uses it at all four cited lines (61, 79, 90, 103). `api/analytics.ts:128`, `api/miro.ts:94`, and `api/workspaces.ts:157` likewise use `seg()`. The guard is additionally applied throughout `api/workspaces.ts` (49, 76, 89, 103, 116, 131, 144, 185, 197, 213, 228, 273, 292, 305, 317, 340), `api/datasources.ts` (46, 66, 79, 91, 105), `api/files.ts:23`, and `app/spreadsheet/image-upload.ts:48`. A repo-wide grep for `VITE_BACKEND_API_URL` in packages/frontend/src shows the only remaining un-`seg`-wrapped interpolations are static route literals with no id substitution (e.g. `/auth/refresh`, `/auth/me`, `/documents/move`, `/documents/delete`, `/notifications/stream`, `/analytics/enabled`) or base-URL constants. The claimed absence is contradicted at every cited file:line.
